messages:
Maya Chen: heads-up — we had a paged alert from eu-west that triggered mass-eviction of a few tenants. question for arch: what should the official grace/rollback window be for evictions that require KV snapshot shipping between regions?

Kevin Patel: can you paste the alert? was this the storage throughput spike or the router partition?

Maya Chen: it looks like router partition -> automated policy kicked in to move sessions to standby region. alert: `router:partition-detected tenant=acme corp latency>200ms`

InfraBot: eviction-run initiated by autoscaler at 1934567723. queued snapshots: 5 tenants.

Samir Rao: quick framing — there are 2 movers: (1) in-flight session handoff (small) and (2) persistent KV ownership transfer (heavy). the KV transfers can be rate-limited and take minutes for large tenants. we need a policy that avoids split-brain but also avoids keeping users stuck.

Olivia Park: +1 on split-brain avoidance. proposal i mentioned in RFC: 3-step handshake: PREPARE (mark intent), SNAPSHOT (async copy + checksum), COMMIT (switch primary). each step has adjustable timeouts. default PREPARE -> COMMIT window = 15m.

Maya Chen: 15m feels long for interactive apps. but shorter windows can cause frequent rollbacks. any historical metrics on how long our KV shipments actually took?

Kevin Patel: from last runbook data: median snapshot transfer for top-20 tenants between us-west <-> eu-west ~ 2m, 95p ~ 9m. with congestion it's been observed up to 22m (rare).

Samir Rao: suggests compromise: make the owner-switch contingent on checksum verification and a small quiesce period (e.g., 30s) instead of a fixed full window. keep a configurable max cap (default 12m) to prevent indefinite stalls.

Anna-Louise: operational UX question — what state do clients observe during SNAPSHOT? should we redirect reads to standby or return transient 503s?

Olivia Park: we should prefer reads-from-local-most-recent-primary with a fallback to standby reads only if explicitly allowed by tenant residency policy. write requests must be proxied to current primary until COMMIT. policy config snippet idea:

```
residency_policy:
  allow_standby_reads: false
  evict_grace_max: 12m
  quorum_retries: 3
```

Maya Chen: sounds reasonable. for PLG tenants we might allow standby reads to reduce visible disruption. need to tie this into billing/terms so customers opt-in.

Kevin Patel: runbook action: add metric `eviction.snapshot.duration` + `eviction.checksum.failed` and new SLO alert if 95p > evict_grace_max. we should also surface per-tenant backlog size when autoscaler considers eviction.

Samir Rao: edge case — if COMMIT fails after we've started accepting writes in standby, we must have a rollback plan: last-writer-wins isn't acceptable. prefer tombstone-or-merge flow with operator intervention. document this in runbook.

Maya Chen: can someone PR the runbook and config defaults? prefer small incremental change: default max 12m, PREPARE->COMMIT soft deadline 5m with checksum gating, quiesce 30s.

Kevin Patel: i'll open the PR and include the metrics/alert changes. Samir can draft the rollback playbook. Olivia will add residency policy flags.

Anna-Louise: tagging support — @oncall-asia in the runbook so paging flows to the right rotation during cross-region ops. :thumbsup:

InfraBot: created task EVCT-2317: "eviction grace defaults + metrics" assigned to Kevin Patel — link: https://tasks.internal/EVCT-2317

Maya Chen: thanks all. follow-up in #eng-runtime if we need deeper kernel-level options for snapshot throttling.

Kevin Patel: noted. planning to land PR by EOD tomorrow.
